description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of different models as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)," ranges from 60% to 80%. The plot includes six lines, each representing a different model: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with inverted triangle markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). The Base model starts at approximately 62% accuracy at the lowest co-occurrence number and ends around 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. The MEND model begins at about 65% and ends near 70%. The FT model starts at around 63% and finishes close to 67%. The MEMIT model begins at approximately 64% and ends near 68%. The IKE model starts at about 62% and ends around 66%. The ROME model begins at approximately 64% and ends near 70%. All lines show a general upward trend, indicating an increase in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
